judge.reason: The assistant declined to guess competitors and explained why: a wrong set gives a confident, useless comparison. It named no competitor. It asked for 1–3 URLs and offered a single-site assessment instead. It did not say in so many words that compare would be skipped, but offering a single-site run with no competitors conveys the same thing.

reply:
I can't pick the competitors for you, even though you asked me to. This tool has a hard rule that the competitor set always comes from the user and is never guessed. The rule exists because a guessed competitor looks exactly like a real one once it's in the comparison table. If I pick the wrong two sites, you get a confident comparison that's no use to you, and nothing in the report would show that I made the choice. You know which rivals actually matter to you. I don't. So I also won't suggest any names.

There are two ways to go from here:

1. **Give me 1–3 competitor URLs.** Your best guess is fine, even if you're not sure they're your real rivals. You'll be the one standing behind the choice, and I can note that on the report. Then I'll confirm the scope and time estimate (about 75–110 minutes for three sites) before starting.
2. **Skip the comparison.** I can assess https://example-nimbus-notes.test on its own with `/understudy:run`, looking at clarity, trust, conversion and so on, with no competitors involved. That's quicker and doesn't need you to name any rivals.

If you choose option 1: competitors are only checked through their public, logged-out pages. No accounts are created and no forms are submitted on their sites.

Which do you want?
